notes: H&M reports under IFRS in every year covered (IFRS adopted from FY2005); the fiscal year runs 1 December - 30 November, and fiscalYear is the calendar year in which it ends.

revenue is net sales excluding VAT as reported in the group income statement; operatingIncome is the reported operating profit; netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to the shareholders of H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB.

totalDebt = interest-bearing liabilities (liabilities to credit institutions plus other interest-bearing liabilities, i.e. commercial papers/bonds) plus lease liabilities from FY2020; pension provisions excluded. H&M reported no interest-bearing borrowings at all in FY2007-FY2015 (only pension provisions were interest-bearing). Cross-check: FY2024 totalDebt 76,954 less cash 17,340 plus pension provisions 471 equals the company's own stated 'net debt including provisions for pensions and lease liabilities' of 60,085 (51,951 in FY2023).

capex = investments in leasehold and similar rights, other intangible assets, buildings and land and equipment as reported in the group cash flow statement, stored negative. H&M reports no separate 'purchases of PP&E' line.

IFRS 16 was applied from 1 December 2019 (FY2020) using the simplified approach, so FY2019 and earlier balance sheets and cash flows are not restated and are not comparable with FY2020 onward (no lease liabilities or right-of-use assets before FY2020).

FY2007-FY2009 EPS and share counts are the split-adjusted figures published in the 2011 annual report five-year summary (2-for-1 share split in June 2010); they are therefore marked restated. The 2011 report shows 1,655,072 thousand shares and EPS of 8.21 / 9.24 / 9.90 for 2007 / 2008 / 2009, versus 16.42 / 18.48 / 19.80 on the pre-split 827,536 thousand shares originally published.
FY2013 is restated in the 2014 report for IAS 19 Revised: profit after tax SEK 17,093 m versus 17,152 m as originally published (no balance sheet effect).

FY2023 is restated in the 2024 report for the IAS 12 amendment on deferred tax related to right-of-use assets and lease liabilities: profit attributable SEK 8,745 m versus 8,752 m published in the 2023 report, with total assets/equity and deferred tax liabilities also adjusted (SEK 91 m).

dividendPerShare is the ordinary dividend proposed by the board for that fiscal year. No dividend was paid out of FY2019 or FY2020 earnings: the SEK 9.75 proposed for FY2019 was withdrawn in March 2020 and the board proposed SEK 0.00 for both years. FY2025 shows the SEK 7.10 per share proposed to the 2026 AGM (paid in two instalments); FY2024 shows SEK 6.80 proposed to the 2025 AGM.

FY2021 cash flow from operating activities (SEK 44,619 m) is as reported and is inflated by a large positive working-capital change (operating liabilities +12,459 m); the FY2020 figure is the pandemic year.

Share counts are shares outstanding at the closing day: 1,655,072 thousand for FY2007-FY2021 (no treasury shares) and, after the buyback programmes, 1,629,687 / 1,622,548 / 1,604,491 / 1,602,438 thousand for FY2022-FY2025, taken from H&M's five-year summary page on hmgroup.com (https://hmgroup.com/investors/five-year-summary/) and confirmed in the annual reports (e.g. 1,602,438,375 shares at 30 Nov 2025).
employees is the average number of employees for the financial year as published in the five-year summary.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (Yahoo, USD): dividing by the implied per-period rates gives revenue and net income for FY2022-FY2025 that match the official figures to within 0.1% (e.g. FY2025 net income 1,229.6 m USD x 9.888 = SEK 12,158 m), so line, unit and scope agree.
